For sleeping I like beach, wind, water, and night sounds, but there is no way to filter for those tracks that are beach or wind and low brightness. Even if there was, it just plays one with no choice or feedback. The only way to find tracks I like is to keep twiddling the filters and then listen and click details to see the neural effect, brightness, and sound type. Then keep blindly doing that over and over until I stumble into a track I like. 2. There needs to be a way to set up a play list so that it's not just one track playing for 8 hours. It can get repetitive. There is an end to each track and you can hear when it ends and restarts. What I need is the ability to select multiple tracks and have it play one, then the next, then the next etc. I want to be able to set how long before it changes, say 90 minutes, and have it automatically move through the playlist and repeat as needed with the option to shuffle. I need to be able to choose deep sleep racks for the first part of the night and sleep and wake for the later stages, with something to help me wake up at the end. It's also frustrating that every time there is a notification of new tracks since I started a few months ago, there have been no new sleep tracks. There is only one guided sleep track, and the only way to find that out is to keep pressing guided sleep and always getting that one track. Die Bildgebungsdaten (EEG/MRT) beruhen auf rund 40 Personen. Unabhängige Replikationen durch externe Labore sind bisher kaum vorhanden. Gemessen wurde zudem vor allem ein monotoner Laborreaktionstest, nicht die Verbesserung der Arbeit/Leistung/Fokus im Alltag. Die oft beworbenen “119 % mehr Fokus-Gehirnwellen” sind ein EEG-Messwert und kein Beleg für 119 % bessere Konzentration oder Produktivität. Dass sich Hirnaktivität verändert, heißt nicht automatisch, dass man besser arbeitet. Auch die Bewerbung für ADHD stützt sich nur auf Selbstauskünfte zu Aufmerksamkeitsproblemen, nicht auf klinische Diagnosen oder Behandlungsstudien. Also ähnlich wie Globolie-Wirkeinordnungen stattfinden. Dafür dann 90+ € im Jahr?! 12,99 € für schöne Naturgeräusche wären angemessen Der Nutzen im Alltag ist nicht bewiesen. text: Reminders aren't repeating . I paid for this app because I have ADHD and narcolepsy and I needed an app that would remind me in advance of certain tasks and then continue to remind me until I had actually completed it, because I have a tendency to notice an alert, then promptly forget that I had something to do when it turns off. Instead of my alerts repeating indefinitely, or even more than a small handful of times (I just tested it and the 1 minute snooze repeated only 9 times before stopping, I lost the data on the 5 and 10 minute snooze settings, but I've set all of my alarms to 5 min snooze before this). What ends up happening is, for example, the alarm starts going off in the morning for me to wake up, but I don't hear it/consciously register it and then after just a few repeats, it's off completely. So I don't wake up on time, and then when I eventually do, the first thing I see is that the alert went off HOURS ago and stopped. EXTREMELY frustrating. I opened the app today (with not even any pending task notification numbers displayed on the Due badge) at random, only because I'd thought to check it, and had a LONG list of alerts that were all permanently snoozed from as far back as 2 WEEKS AGO, and I was never able to mark them as "done." Because they just turned off on their own. I need alerts to literally repeat until I am ready to turn them off manually. To compensate for this issue I've ended up making ~six different alerts for the same task that I can't afford to forget about at slightly different times. The calendar alert system on iOS only gives me limited options to forewarn me of an event, and once it alerts me once, it doesn't alert me again, and I have to remember to reset the alert as the event gets closer. I really need an app that can do this. This app would be great if the repeat function actually repeated more than a small, set number of times.

app: EndeavorOTC®- Outplay ADHD - Proven Adult ADHD Treatment
text: Doesn't really work— too many game design flaws . I've played this very consistently for four weeks, surpassed my goal focus score, but have seen little to no improvement in my ADHD symptoms. There are numerous game design flaws, particularly with the algorithm that supposedly makes it a treatment, that undermine the treatment potential for any functional adult. 1) It is designed so that you graduate to increasingly difficult worlds as you progress. Great— except I beat all the game content in 2 weeks, and am now stuck repeating the same missions over and over— erasing the possibility of fostering neuroplasticity. 2) The game design is lacking both creativity and detailed attention to the point of it becoming ineffective. Mainly I'm talking about the visual targets—- where color is the main differentiator it's okay, but half the game also depends on identifying objects by shape— but some objects look similar to most others while a couple have distinct shapes— which would be fine if the algorithm that calculates your scores and modulates difficulty knew this— but it doesn't. I can predict whether I'll pass a mission and whether my “selectivity” and “reaction time” will be high or low based on which object is selected for that mission— if it's one that blends in the mission becomes more difficult but the algorithm doesn't realize this 3) The function of the algorithm is too obvious — the game speeds up and slows down in a terribly jerky fashion every time you hit several targets in a row, or miss one, respectively. 4) It is supposed to limit you to 25 minutes a day— but the amount it subtracts from daily timer is often incorrect by a minute. The game has the gaul to scold me for playing only 22 minutes per day (the number varies) when in fact I played until the game stopped me each day consistently. It doesn't make sense 5) Again, I'm more distracted and addicted to my phone than before i started this “treatment.” MAYBE my visual processing is a hair better. If I had never played a video game maybe it would have caused adaptive changes … but it didn't. I think the product has potential but the game feels extremely incomplete, and at best in alpha or beta testing phase. Save your money until they have competitors and game design has been completed in a couple years.

They enroll 221 adults to test the product, but did not have a control group that did not access the product. So there's zero evidence that the change was caused by the product. My personal experience is that I used this app daily for 6 weeks and I can't say I felt an improvement in my attention.

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: NOT for neurodivergent IMO . I really wanted to like this app because it has a great reputation for people like myself, but the onboarding completely lost me. The review is a little long but it's worth the read. The biggest issue wasn't the goals themselves. It was that the app immediately requires you to start making choices before you can explore or do anything else. There isn't an option to simply explore the app, learn how it works, or ease into the experience first. Instead, it essentially says, “Select this to continue,” with no alternative path forward. For people with anxiety, burnout, or some neurodivergent people, getting started is often the hardest part. I downloaded the app because I needed help with that, and the onboarding didn't support that for me. Don't immediately ask me to do the very thing I'm struggling to do. It felt like signing up to learn horseback riding and, instead of introducing you to the horse or explaining the basics, someone immediately hands you the reins and says, “Here's your trail.” I don't need endless customization. I just wanted another path, like a brief introduction or walkthrough before getting started. Let me get comfortable before telling me where I'm going. Another thing that also disappointed me was the advertising. The ads gave me the impression there would be a more in-depth questionnaire to personalize my experience, but I never found one. I was also surprised to see the app marketed as being helpful for people with ADHD and other neurodivergent users because, as someone in that audience, the onboarding didn't feel designed with my experience in mind. That approach may work well for many people, including neurotypical people, but for me it increased my anxiety instead of my motivation. If an app is designed to help people with motivation and action, it shouldn't assume everyone is ready to act the moment they open it. Some of us seeking help need help taking that very first step. I truly hope the developers consider offering 2 onboarding paths: one for users who are ready to jump right in, and another for users who need a little time to understand the app before getting started. I think that small change could make the app more accessible to an entirely different group of people and help more users succeed. For many of us, simply opening the app for growth is already the first victory. Meeting users where they are, instead of where they hope to be, could help more people continue the journey and ultimately succeed. Unfortunately for me, this wasn't a neurodivergent-friendly onboarding experience.

text: GET HABITICA INSTEAD . TL;DR: The app itself is great, but the updates are never properly tested before release, so it's always buggy and broken. This app often breaks and becomes very difficult to use after an update, so much so that I cringe when I see it updating. It's almost as if no testing gets done before release. Use a different app if you're an adult with ADHD or you plan to use it to manage your entire to-do list. (Habitica is great!) It's just not going to be there to help you every day. *Edit in response to the developer response:* Trust me, I have, way too often, and almost always because of a bug caused by an update. No other app in my phone has me emailing support as often as this one. So I'D appreciate if I could trust it to work. *Update* I've been trying for three weeks to get a bug from 2.0.0 fixed. The bug did not get fixed in the 2.1.0 update even though I was told it was being fixed. This bug is causing old, completed one time tasks to remain stuck in the Any time order list, and I can't access them from another tab to delete them. In fact, some of these old tasks could be described as zombies, because tasks I completed in OCTOBER reappeared. Since the 2.0.0 update, the list has gotten longer and longer as I complete more tasks and they don't disappear/can't be deleted from the reordering list. text: Strange, Depressing App . Instead, after using Routinery, I found myself more bound to the unnatural rigidness of tech than I ever thought I'd be. Meaning, the structure this app encourages is at odds with human lifestyles. Beyond including a pause button, it doesn't offer the ability to handle variance in your life. It insists on a structure that you feel bound to, as if an overbearing boss strapped a tracking device to your hand and asked that you manage your time according to the needs of the business. Sure, you are in control of your needs with this app, you designate how you spend your time. Though, I could see a negative psychological response for many who use this app as for those of us with severe focus issues, straying from the structure of time this app demands could become stressful and therefore discouraging. It did for me. I highly recommend a standard time-blocking method and encouraging yourself to stick to the structure through reminders and in others ways that are unique to your needs. Also, the Dwayne Johnson and Kim Kardashian routine examples are cringey and odd to incorporate into an app. The experience for me has been a bit depressing. It allowed for technology to become far too heavy of a hand in my routine and I'm happy I no longer use it.

text: Unfortunately, not ADHD friendly . I'm just letting this warning here because it was nowhere to be found before I purchased the app: they REMOVED THE “ROUTINE” FUNCTION in some update, despite promoting this feature in all of their communications. That said, this really doesn't matter AS MUCH, since you can still create one activity called, let's say… “Morning Routine” and have subtasks on it. But as an ADHDer myself, this app has 2 flaws that I simply cannot understand, even more on an app that is made by and for us neurodivergents: 1) it “punishes” you if you are late for any activity 2) it does not allow to enter activities with a due date+time, but without a defined duration. Let me explain: 1) ALL activities have an individual and automatic timer, that starts at the due date/time an it is great to be able to see the activity and the time passing by in real time WHEN YOU CAN MAKE IT ON TIME. Because if you, for some reason are late, you CANNOT STOP IT, or even edit it. Only pause it. Also, if you accidentally tap on the “play” button right above an activity, you cannot undo it. For both cases (activity already started or accidentally tap on “play” button), you have to delete the activity and re-insert it! Let me give an example: I had a swimming class today on my Google Calendar at 10AM but the teacher couldn't make it and just told me after 10AM. Tiimo has an integration with GC, so it imported the event, but right at 10pm the timer started to roll until 11am, automatically! You cannot edit ANY event, the imported and/or the ones we create originally in app, AFTER it starts. I wrote an email about all I'm writing here, and they've confirmed: I have to DELETE the activity and re-insert it again, with the new date/time. And if the activity was imported from GC, I have to go out of the app, go to Google Calendar, delete and re-enter the event with the new date+time. That's more time wasting and more opportunities to make mistakes and forget things… 2) Another big flaw for me is that we cannot create activities/events without a defined duration. Let's say I want to wash my dishes at 2PM, but I don't know how much time it takes yet. We all know “time blindness” is a struggle for us with ADHD and Autism! But in this app, instead, I have to create an activity on the day I want and leave it as “any time of the day” option, and remember that I need to do it by 2PM myself. That's right, a planning app in which you have to use your own memory (and we all know how bad our memories are, that's why we look for apps in the first place)… They give us another workaround, that is to create the “washing dishes” task with an approximate duration and DURING THE ACTIVITY, keep tapping the “+” icon to add more minutes. With my hands wet?! And if I was on my swimming class and it was longer than it usually is? I have to leave the pool running and go to the app to add more time before the class ends? How frustrating it is, to set an arbitrary time for something, like “editing a video”, and have to pause the activity itself to get the phone and keep adding minutes? How distracting and disappointing it is? So, basically, I need to pay for this app and for another one like Toggl to first track the time I take to do every single activity in my life and then use Tiimo. That doesn't make sense. And another consequence of this, is that I cannot have on the same app, my tasks/activities and basic reminders, like someone's birthday or holiday! If you import a “moon phase” or any calendar I just mentioned to Tiimo that is just an reminder for the day (and not a task per se), you have to set a timing duration or it will be together with the “anytime” tasks during the day. I just don't understand… so now I have to pay for Tiimo, Toggl and have to leave the app and enter on my Calendar app to see “all day” events that aren't tasks, like “credit card due date”, or “Easter”. That's the perfect recipe for failure as someone who struggles with focus and attention! _ So, to summarize, on Tiimo, I have the following results by the end of my day: • A swimming lesson that I supposedly did, but in reality didn't; • A pile of dishes in the sink, that I now have to wash in the evening when I am out of energy and tired, because I couldn't guess the duration, so the task went to the “anytime” tab, that was closed to avoid distractions from the main ones; • A full afternoon supposedly without any activity, because I needed to use another app to track the time I took to edit a video, so that I can add it more accurately on Tiimo the next time; • Oh, and I forgot to call my friend on her birthday, because I couldn't add this event on Tiimo without a task attached to it and didn't entered my Calendar app today _ I know the creator's intentions are good, so I don't plan on lashing out here. I really have tried the workarounds, but all I did was waste my money and patience. I'll be testing Tick-Tick now, since they have all the functions mentioned, a minimalist layout and widgets way more useful!

It absolutely has potential, but its currently too flawed, disorganized, complex, visually unappealing to be worth using imo. 1. My Day and Library don't seem to be synced, in that deleting something in one doesn't delete it in the other, so theres no actual way to see a list of all of your routines & activities. 2. Editing an activity in the Library will create a duplicate in both the library and the day planner which you have to individually delete. 3. Editing a routine in My Day will create a duplicate in My Day that doesn't show up in the routine Library. 4. There's no separation between repeating activities/routines and one time activities/routines in the Library, so activities like “feed the cat” or “do laundry” will be mixed in with “watch star wars” or “stitch hole in jeans” from 3 months ago. It's more of a history tab than a library. 5. Activities and Routines take up an unnecessary amount of space in My Day to the point where you can only see maybe 2 on your screen at once. Routines particularly have huge chunks of unnecessary empty space both when theyre expanded and when theyre collapsed. 6. No transition between activities & routines in My Day. Its just block after block. An example of good visual transitions between events can be found in an app called Structured, which will remain my primary app despite having less features. 7. You can only ever see the plan for one day at a time, ie theres no way to get a glance at the coming week (i expected this to appear in the top bar of the My Day page when i added tasks but it didn't) 8.
